name: MO-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+27 partisan lean in a heavily Republican Missouri district
Smith's $5M war chest vs. Reichard's ~$6K raised
Incumbent Smith running for re-election with no contested general-election polling
model.rationale: Jason Smith is a well-funded incumbent in a district with a 27-point Republican lean, while Democrat Chris Reichard has raised only about $5,700. Markets price Smith near 96%, and no polling or expert ratings suggest any competitive threat.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or unexpected statewide Missouri swing could tighten the margin, though nothing in the evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
MO-08 covers rural southern Missouri, one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the state, with a partisan lean of about 27 points toward the GOP. Jason Smith, the incumbent and a senior House Republican, is running for re-election with more than $5 million on hand. His Democratic opponent, Chris Reichard, has raised under $6,000, and a Libertarian is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings track this race, and prediction markets give Smith roughly a 96% chance of winning. With such a large financial and structural advantage, the race is rated Safe Republican, with an expected margin in the low twenties.
